claim: Both SNS FIFO topics and Kinesis Streams let you build applications that require strictly ordered, many-to-many messaging.
question: When should I use SNS FIFO topics and when should I use Kinesis Data Streams?

values.display: SNS FIFO topics and Kinesis Streams

evidence.quote: Both SNS FIFO topics and Kinesis Streams enable you to build applications that require strictly ordered, many-to-many messaging.

claim: SNS FIFO topics support use cases that require large ordered fan-out, up to 100 subscribers.
question: How many subscribers can an SNS FIFO topic fan out to in order?

evidence.quote: SNS FIFO topics can further unlock application integration use cases that require large ordered fan-out, up to 100 subscribers.

claim: Kinesis Streams supports ordered fan-out up to 5 subscribers and is often used for analytics and anomaly detection use cases.
question: How many subscribers does Kinesis Streams support for ordered fan-out?

evidence.quote: Kinesis Streams, on the other hand, supports ordered fan-out up to 5 subscribers and is often used for analytics and anomaly detection use cases.

note: SNS FAQ wording. Compare with the Kinesis Data Streams guide (chapter 34) before writing the number.

claim: By default, SNS offers 10 million subscriptions per topic. To request a higher quota, contact Support.
question: How many subscriptions can an SNS topic have?

evidence.quote: By default, SNS offers 10 million subscriptions per topic, and 100,000 topics per account. To request a higher quota, please contact Support.

note: FAQ wording. The General Reference quota table lists 12,500,000 subscriptions per standard topic and 100 per FIFO topic; the guide and quota table are current truth.

claim: By default, SNS offers 100,000 topics per account. To request a higher quota, contact Support.
question: How many topics can an AWS account have in Amazon SNS?

evidence.quote: By default, SNS offers 10 million subscriptions per topic, and 100,000 topics per account. To request a higher quota, please contact Support.

note: FAQ wording. The General Reference quota table separates standard topics (100,000) from FIFO topics (1,000).

claim: By default, 200 filter policies per account per Region can be applied to a topic, according to the FAQ.
question: How many message filters can be applied to a topic?

values.display: 200 filter policies per account per region

evidence.quote: By default, 200 filter policies per account per region can be applied to a topic.

note: FAQ wording. The General Reference lists 200 filter policies per topic and 10,000 per account; compare before writing.

claim: Topic names are limited to 256 characters. Alphanumeric characters plus hyphens (-) and underscores (_) are allowed.
question: How long can an Amazon SNS topic name be?

values.display: Alphanumeric characters plus hyphens (-) and underscores (_)

evidence.quote: Topic names are limited to 256 characters. Alphanumeric characters plus hyphens (-) and underscores (_) are allowed.

claim: The default maximum size of an Amazon SNS message is 256 KiB.
question: What is the default maximum size of an Amazon SNS message?

evidence.quote: The default maximum is 256 KiB, including XML, JSON and unformatted text.

note: The 1 MiB opt-in (see sns-faq-message-size-up-to-1-mib-opt-in) is new; older exam questions assume 256 KB.

claim: With the exception of SMS messages, an Amazon SNS message can contain up to 1 MiB of text data when you set the MaximumMessageSize topic attribute.
question: How large can an Amazon SNS message be?

values.display: up to 1 MiB of text data

evidence.quote: With the exception of SMS messages, Amazon SNS messages can contain up to 1 MiB of text data, by setting the MaximumMessageSize topic attribute.

note: Not examinable yet: the SNS 1 MiB support was announced 2026-09-18, after the 2026-07-15 cut-off.

claim: Each 64KB chunk of published data is billed as 1 request. A single API call with a 1 MiB payload is billed as 16 requests.
question: How is a large Amazon SNS payload billed?

evidence.quote: Each 64KB chunk of published data is billed as 1 request. For example, a single API call with a 1 MiB payload will be billed as 16 requests.

claim: Amazon SNS users pay $0.50 per 1 million requests, $0.06 per 100,000 notification deliveries over HTTP, and $2.00 per 100,000 notification deliveries over email.
question: How much does Amazon SNS cost?

evidence.quote: Users pay $0.50 per 1 million Amazon SNS Requests, $0.06 per 100,000 notification deliveries over HTTP, and $2.00 per 100,000 notification deliveries over email.

claim: Each month, Amazon SNS customers incur no charges for the first 1 million requests, the first 100,000 notifications over HTTP, and the first 1,000 notifications over email.
question: What does the Amazon SNS Free Tier include?

evidence.quote: Each month, Amazon SNS customers incur no charges for the first 1 million Amazon SNS requests, no charges for the first 100,000 notifications over HTTP, and no charges for the first 1,000 notifications over email.

claim: The token in the confirmation message sent to an endpoint on a subscription request is valid for 2 days.
question: How long will subscription requests remain pending, while waiting to be confirmed?

evidence.quote: Token included in the confirmation message sent to end-points on a subscription request are valid for 2 days.

claim: The explicit opt-in confirmation steps are not required when you subscribe your Amazon SQS queue to your Amazon SNS topic and both are owned by the same AWS account.
question: Does subscribing an SQS queue to an SNS topic need a confirmation?

evidence.quote: Note: The explicit “opt-in” steps described above are not required for the specific case where you subscribe your Amazon SQS queue to your Amazon SNS topic – and both are “owned” by the same AWS account.

claim: If the user who owns the SQS queue is not the owner of the SNS topic, Amazon SNS requires an explicit confirmation of the subscription request.
question: What happens when the owner of an SQS queue differs from the owner of the SNS topic it subscribes to?

values.display: not the owner of the topic

evidence.quote: If the user owning the SQS queue is not the owner of the topic, Amazon SNS will require an explicit confirmation to the subscription request.

claim: By default, only topic owners have permissions to publish to an SNS topic. A topic owner can set explicit permissions to allow more than one user to publish.
question: Can multiple users publish to a single topic?

values.display: only topic owners have permissions to publish

evidence.quote: A topic owner can set explicit permissions to allow more than one user (with a valid AWS ID) to publish to a topic. By default, only topic owners have permissions to publish to a topic.

claim: The AddPermission and RemovePermission APIs give a simple way to add and remove topic permissions. For conditional access and more advanced use cases, use access control policies.
question: How can the owner grant or revoke publish or subscribe permissions on a topic?

values.display: conditional access and more advanced use cases

evidence.quote: The AddPermission and RemovePermission APIs provide a simple interface for developers to add and remove permissions for a topic. However, for conditional access and more advanced use cases, users should use access control policies to manage permissions.

claim: Only the owner of the topic can change permissions for that topic.
question: Who can change permissions on a topic?

values.display: Only the owner of the topic

evidence.quote: Only the owner of the topic can change permissions for that topic.

claim: By default, SNS delivers messages encoded in JSON that provides metadata about the message and topic. You can opt in to raw delivery, where messages arrive exactly as published.
question: What is the default behavior if the raw message delivery property on the subscription is not set?

values.display: By default, messages are delivered encoded in JSON

evidence.quote: You can opt-in to get your messages delivered in raw form, i.e. exactly as you published them. By default, messages are delivered encoded in JSON that provides metadata about the message and topic.

claim: You can set the raw message delivery property of an SNS subscription in the console or with the SetSubscriptionAttributes API.
question: How do I enable raw message delivery in Amazon SNS?

evidence.quote: This property can be set by using the AWS Management Console, or by using the API SetSubscriptionAttributes.

claim: Raw message delivery is supported with SQS and HTTP(S) endpoints. Deliveries to Lambda, email, and SMS endpoints behave the same regardless of the RawMessageDelivery property.
question: Which types of endpoints support raw message delivery?

values.display: supported with SQS and HTTP(S) endpoints

evidence.quote: Raw message delivery support is supported with SQS and HTTP(S) endpoints. Deliveries to Lambda, email, and SMS endpoints will behave the same independent of the “RawMessageDelivery” property.

claim: You can subscribe your own Lambda functions to an SNS topic that another account created, as long as the topic policy allows it.
question: Can I subscribe AWS Lambda functions created by someone else to Amazon SNS topics that I own?

values.display: topic policy for that SNS topic allows it

evidence.quote: You can subscribe your own AWS Lambda functions to your own Amazon SNS topics or subscribe your AWS Lambda functions to an Amazon SNS topic that was created by another account so long as the topic policy for that SNS topic allows it.

note: The same FAQ answer says an account owner cannot subscribe a Lambda function of another account; that older sentence is not recorded as a fact.

claim: If AWS Lambda throttles an Amazon SNS message, Amazon SNS retries the delivery attempts.
question: What happens when Lambda throttles an SNS delivery?

evidence.quote: If AWS Lambda throttles an Amazon SNS message, Amazon SNS will retry the delivery attempts.
